status: Shared visual capture allocations now obey process GPU admission and tracked completion lifetimes; full resource acceptance remains open

behavior: One Datum-owned capture resource module reserves actual four-byte texture extents and padded readback capacity against the existing 512 MiB process GPU limit before API allocation. Existing RGBA/BGRA formats, output pixels and row padding are preserved.

Both render and copy submissions hold charged resources through completion, including an early render/readback error and warm rendering without a readback. Independent capture owners appear in the existing process allocation registry.
Readback is not upload staging; its capacity is classified as Readback and charged to the GPU process total. No new subcap or changes to the default renderer path.

proof.lint_build: Strict visual renderer/app all-targets Clippy and fresh visual application build pass. Source health 2268, dependency authority and governance gates pass. Initial Clippy exposed a raw-texture test helper; migrated that helper to the shared owner and preserved the failed log.
proof.scope: No native input or benchmark campaign. Prior Console golden discrepancy remains unresolved; full drift not rerun.

limits: Only the existing four-byte RGBA/BGRA visual capture formats are supported; driver residency, CPU image allocations, internal API metadata and broader accounting/qualification remain separate.

This closes a feature-gated capture allocation bypass, not full MEM-GPU-TOTAL/ACC-01, S4/S5 or issue acceptance. GEFN, nonblocking resize and concurrent multi-device qualification boundaries remain unchanged.
No dependency, vendoring, license, prototype, numerical budget or specification amendment.
